title: Start to surrender in about 38 minutes.
description:
Start to surrender in about 38 minutes. 27 August 1896, between the British Empire and the island sultanate of Zanzibar. The whole conflict was over before an hour had passed.

He seized the throne when the pro-British sultan died suddenly. Britain ordered him out by 9am on 27 August. He refused, and barricaded the palace with some 3,000 men.

By 09:40 the flag was down. Within two minutes most of Khalid's guns were wrecked and he had slipped out a back door. The shelling did the rest.

The length of the war by the usual count; a few sources say closer to 40. Either way, long enough to leave the palace in rubble.

About 500 hit on one side. One on the other. Over 500 of Khalid's men were killed or wounded. The only British casualty was a single petty officer: injured, and he recovered.

Sources:
- https://www.historic-uk.com/HistoryUK/HistoryofBritain/The-Shortest-War-in-History/: Historic UK (Ben Johnson), read directly: the Anglo-Zanzibar War of 27 August 1896 is generally considered the shortest in history at 38 minutes; Khalid bin Barghash seized the throne after Sultan Hamad bin Thuwaini died on 25 Aug 1896; Britain's ultimatum expired at 9am on 27 Aug; the bombardment began at 9am, by 09:02 most of Khalid's artillery was destroyed and he had fled, by 09:40 the flag was down; ~3,000 defenders; over 500 of Khalid's men killed or wounded; one British petty officer severely injured but he recovered.
- https://www.britannica.com/event/Anglo-Zanzibar-War: Encyclopaedia Britannica, read directly (summary and Quick Facts): dates the war to 27 August 1896 and states it 'lasted no longer than 40 minutes, making it the shortest war in recorded history'; British cruisers fired on Khalid ibn Barghash's position.
